record.paper_title: Symmetric Functions in Superspace: A Compendium of Results and Open Problems (Including a SageMath Worksheet)
record.original_question: Let J_Λ(q,t)=h_Λ^{lo}(q,t)P_Λ(q,t) be the integral form of the Macdonald superpolynomial, let φ_t be the automorphism defined by φ_t(p_r)=(1-t^r)^{-1}p_r and φ_t(~p_s)=~p_s, and let H_Λ(q,t)=φ_t(J_Λ(q,t)). When H_Λ(q,t) is expanded in the Schur-superpolynomial basis as H_Λ(q,t)=Σ_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q,t)s_Ω, are all coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients?

evidence.quote: The integral form associated to the super-Macdonald P_Λ(q, t) is given by (4.70) J_Λ(q, t) = h^{lo}_Λ(q, t)P_Λ(q, t).

Let φ_t be the automorphism of A determined by (4.71) φ_t(p_r) = (1 − t^r)^{−1} p_r, (r ≥ 1); φ_t(~p_s) = ~p_s, (s ≥ 0), and then define the modified Macdonald superpolynomial H_Λ(q, t) as (4.72) H_Λ(q, t) = φ_t(J_Λ(q, t)).
The expansion of H_Λ(q, t) in the Schur superpolynomial basis s_Ω (see (4.15)) defines the (q, t)-Kostka coefficients, (4.73) H_Λ(q, t) = ∑_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q, t) s_Ω
Conjecture 4.3 – (Positivity). [23] The coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q, t) are, for all superpartitions Λ and Ω, polynomials in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients, that is, they belong to N[q, t].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the algebra A of symmetric functions in superspace over Q(q,t), generated by the commuting power sums p_r (r ≥ 1) and the anticommuting power sums ~p_s (s ≥ 0). Symmetric functions in superspace are indexed by superpartitions Λ = (Λ^a; Λ^s), where Λ^a is a strict partition of distinct nonnegative parts (the "anticommuting" sector) and Λ^s is an ordinary partition.

Let {P_Λ(q,t)}_Λ denote the Macdonald superpolynomials, the basis of A characterized by suitable triangularity and orthogonality with respect to the (q,t)-deformed scalar product on superspace. Let h_Λ^{lo}(q,t) be the "lower-hook" normalization factor, and define the integral form
   J_Λ(q,t) = h_Λ^{lo}(q,t) · P_Λ(q,t).

Let φ_t : A → A be the Q(q,t)-algebra automorphism determined by
   φ_t(p_r) = (1 − t^r)^{−1} p_r  for all r ≥ 1,   φ_t(~p_s) = ~p_s  for all s ≥ 0,
and define the modified Macdonald superpolynomial
   H_Λ(q,t) = φ_t( J_Λ(q,t) ).

Let {s_Ω}_Ω denote the Schur superpolynomial basis of A. Expand
   H_Λ(q,t) = Σ_Ω K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) · s_Ω,
defining the (q,t)-Kostka coefficients K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) in superspace.

Prove or disprove: for every pair of superpartitions Λ and Ω, the coefficient K_{ΩΛ}(q,t) lies in N[q,t], i.e. is a polynomial in q and t with nonnegative integer coefficients.
artifact.status_search_result: The (q,t)-Kostka positivity conjecture for Macdonald superpolynomials was formulated by Blondeau-Fournier, Desrosiers, Lapointe, and Mathieu (2012), generalizing Macdonald's classical positivity (proved by Haiman, 2001) to superspace. Searches for proofs through 2024–2025 turn up only restatements of the conjecture, partial/related results (e.g. nonnegativity of stable-limit double Macdonald (q,t)-Kostka coefficients and Schur-positivity in special cases), but no proof of the full superspace positivity statement. The conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Macdonald polynomials in superspace: conjectural definition and positivity conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Presents a conjectural definition of Macdonald polynomials in superspace and formulates positivity conjectures for the (q,t)-Kostka coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Original formulation of the superspace (q,t)-Kostka positivity conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Double Macdonald polynomials as the stable limit of Macdonald superpolynomials
status_evidence.snippet: Validates conjectures in the stable regime and shows certain (q,t)-Kostka coefficients are q,t-analogs of dimensions of irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group.
status_evidence.claim: Partial/stable-limit results, but the full superspace positivity remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert schemes, polygraphs and the Macdonald positivity conjecture (Haiman)
status_evidence.snippet: Haiman's proof of the classical Macdonald positivity conjecture via the n! theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Classical (non-super) analog is solved; the superspace version is the conjectural extension.
